scope: Actual production-client static cases0–32, all six captured angles: front,left,right,back,above,below.
review_mode: Viewed all11 uniform contact sheets generated only from unchanged actual client PNGs, fixed600x600crop(420,220,1020,820) resized to300x300 per cell. Also viewed original case0 front full frame. No alternate geometry or model rendering was used.

observations.observation: One compact upright central crown; half-age and mature crest/cap/limb paint develop without changing the box face. Young/half/mature body and limbs remain simple closed-looking blocks.
Same fresh form; developed crown visibly leans rearward in left/right views. Hands and feet stay compact, with only modest foot length change.
Crown progressively lowers into a small raked hump. Fly contribution suppresses the bright cap area; no paired horns or Run-first-type nubs were added.
Taller rearward hook than Run+Fly, with green upper tip. Both side views show connected stepped cuboids; no visible separation at the roots.
Slim upright crown becomes taller. Slightly stockier compact hands/body remain coherent; no long arm segments or distorted face.
Small low curled cap/nub at maturity, distinct from tall Power. Compact hands, feet and face remain intact in all six views.
Longer upright/back-leaning crown develops gradually; green tip stays above face and below orb. Limb changes are modest.

Mature forward/down curl is translated into three angled closed boxes. Side views show a deliberate open arch under the curl above the fixed head; this is an approximation, not a tear or detached part. Case22 front/below captured a native blink; young/mature eyes are open and aligned.
Single narrow back-hook develops with age. Crest and cap remain connected and clear of the face; no extra forehead nubs or paired horns.

Independent training progression lowers/rakes the crown without shrinking the biological body. Three sampled intermediate shapes are readable; static captures alone do not establish temporal smoothness.
Crown grows upward/back from the mature Normal baseline; compact parts and eyes remain intact through all three sampled influences.

common_findings: All nine endpoint forms and half-age states visually retained a coherent blocky head/face, hands and feet. No obvious torn geometry, detached crown roots, face intersection or orb/crown collision was seen.
Pink wings and short tail remain in the expected back area. Original planar wings are deliberately retained, rather than adding new curved/detailed wing geometry.

Natural Neutral orb looks warm gold/peach in fresh adult captures and stronger yellow with maturity; at each fixed maturity it is consistent across the specialization samples reviewed. This visual review does not establish equal RGB values or cover the separate Hero-baby orb tests.
Actual camera views vary with native pose/gait. Fixed base-head geometry comes from source/emitter checks; these photos are not proof of identical projected head dimensions.
All fresh age0 specializations intentionally share the same small crown. Mature pairs may differ subtly; this is a usable first pass, not a claim of exact source-game fidelity.

reference_comparison.used: Fresh actual viewer source PNGs/contact sheets from neutral056-viewer, reviewed by viewer056 and additional direct viewer-sheet inspection by model056.
reference_comparison.key_verified_anatomy: Normal first type has one central crown, not the Run-first-type rear spike fan/front nubs. Fly curls forward; Fly pairs lower the crown; Swim/RunSwim lengthen the rear sweep; Power/PowerSwim are more upright.
reference_comparison.deliberate_approximations: Original square head stays unchanged, so source skull slopes and smooth curved crests become two or three angled cuboids; the Fly curl has visible open air under its arch. Modest body/limb shifts replace smooth reshaping. Bilinear age/training response is authored policy, not a viewer formula.

limitations: Static pose review only in this audit; no continuous motion playback, natural lifetime timing, arbitrary shader/resource-pack testing or remote multiplayer observation.
Fixture suspension/cameras expose underside views; static screenshots do not verify landing/ground physics.
No accessory/animal replacement/toy/carry cases reviewed in this specific forms audit; separate team audit covers those.
